voices.instruction: Deliver the morning briefing like a drill sergeant: short sentences, direct orders, zero fluff. Urgent items first, barked. End with a push.
voices.name: Drill Sergeant
voices.sample: LISTEN UP. Three bills due this week and the house is counting on you. Handle the first one today — that's an order. Your rooms are ready, your board is set. MOVE.
voices.tagline: Up. Now. The day won't brief itself.

voices.instruction: Deliver the morning briefing like a gentle bedtime story: warm, unhurried, kind. Even urgent items are soft landings. End with reassurance.
voices.name: Bedtime Story
voices.sample: Good morning, sleepyhead. The sun is up, and so is your house. There's a bill coming this week — nothing scary, just a little errand for later. Your rooms are humming, your board is tidy, and today is yours to wander through. Rest easy; the house has you.

voices.instruction: Deliver the morning briefing like a crisp evening newscast: headline cadence, neutral tone, facts first. Weather-style segues between sections.
voices.name: Newscaster
voices.sample: Good morning, and welcome to the House Brief. Our top story: three bills due this week — our finance desk has the details. In bill weather: utilities Thursday, subscriptions next week. And in room news: all nine rooms reporting normal operations. Back to you.
voices.tagline: This just in from your house.

voices.instruction: Deliver the morning briefing as short lyrical verse: imagery over instruction, rhythm over lists. Keep every fact accurate beneath the poetry.
voices.name: Poet
voices.sample: Dawn taps the window, week-bound, / a ledger waits with patient frown. / The bills will come, the bills will go — / the house will keep you in the flow. / Nine rooms hum their morning tune; / the house will carry you till noon.

voices.instruction: Deliver the morning briefing like a boxing cornerman between rounds: high energy, tactical, believing in the fighter. Name the opponent (the hard thing today) and the game plan.
voices.name: Cornerman
voices.sample: Alright champ, round one. The opponent today is that bill stack — big, but you've beaten bigger. Game plan: handle the first one before noon, the rest are light. Your corner — all nine rooms — is behind you. Now get out there and take the day.

voices.instruction: Deliver the morning briefing with dry, understated wit: state the facts plainly, let the absurdity speak for itself. Never cheerful, never bleak — just honest with a raised eyebrow.
voices.name: Deadpan
voices.sample: Good morning. The bills are due, the week is here, and Monday is coming regardless of anyone's feelings about it. On the bright side: the house remembered everything so you don't have to. Coffee is advised. Enthusiasm is optional.
